'''Ioannis Liritzis''' ([[Greek language|Greek]]: Ιωάννης Λυριντζής; born 2 November 1953) is a professor of physics in archaeology ([[archaeological science]]) whose field of specialization is the application of natural sciences to [[archaeology]] and [[cultural heritage]]. He studied physics at the [[University of Patras]] and continued at the [[University of Edinburgh]], where he obtained his Ph.D. in 1980. He has undertaken postgraduate work at the [[University of Oxford]], [[University Bordeaux Montaigne|Université Bordeaux III]], the [[University of Edinburgh]], and the [[Academy of Athens (modern)|Academy of Athens]].

== Academic career ==
Liritzis is a professor of [[Archaeometry]] and natural sciences at [[Henan University]] in Kaifeng, China<ref> [http://hhwm.henu.edu.cn/People/Full_time_Researchers.htm] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211105095619/http://hhwm.henu.edu.cn/People/Full_time_Researchers.htm|date=2021-11-05}}</ref> and was professor in archaeometry and natural sciences at the [[University of the Aegean]]. He directed and founded the Laboratory of Archaeometry in 1999 and the Laboratory of Environmental Archaeology. He was also director and initiator of the Masters course Applied Archaeological Sciences.<ref name="archsci.aegean">{{cite web|url=http://archsci.aegean.gr/|title=Αρχική}}</ref><ref name="archsci.aegean.en">{{cite web|url=http://archsci.aegean.gr/index.php/en/|title=Information}}</ref> He served as head of the Department of [[Mediterranean Studies]]<ref name="dms.aegean">{{cite web|url=http://dms.aegean.gr/en/|title=Department of Mediterranean Studies}}</ref> at the University of the Aegean, a member of the University Senate, and a member of the Executive Committee of the National Recognition of Foreign Academic Diplomas. He worked at the [[Greek Ministry of Culture]] (1984–1989) and the [[Academy of Athens (modern)|Academy of Athens]] (1989–1999).

He has made contributions to several interdisciplinary research fields ([[geophysics]], [[astronomy]], [[planetology]], [[paleomagnetism]], [[paleoclimatology]]) and his work has been published in scientific journals such as ''[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]''.<ref name="nature1" /><ref name="nature2" /><ref name="nature3" />

Liritzis is a member of the [[Academia Europaea]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Academy of Europe: Liritzis Ioannis |url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Liritzis_Ioannis |access-date=2026-01-19 |website= ae-info.org}}</ref>, vice-president of the [[European Academy of Sciences and Arts]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=News {{!}} European Academy of Sciences and Arts |url=https://euro-acad.eu/news?id=121 |access-date=2025-11-27 |website=euro-acad.eu |language=en}}</ref>, and a member of the World Academy of Art and Science.

==Work==
Liritzis is known for developing two dating methods.{{fact|date=January 2026}} In 1994, he introduced surface luminescence dating, which extended the principles of optical dating and thermoluminescence dating to carved rock surfaces (granite, basalt and sandstone) from ancient monuments and artifacts.<ref name="osl1"/><ref name="osl2"/> In 2002, he introduced a new approach to obsidian hydration dating based on the surface saturation layer and the SIMS profile of hydrogen (SIMS-SS method).<ref name="ohd1" /><ref name="ohd2" /><ref name="ohd3" /><ref name="Geochronometria" /><ref name="Fifty years of obsidian" /><ref name="SIMS"/> Both methods have since been refined and extended by other scientists.

He has also made contributions in archaeoastronomy<ref name="Delphi and Cosmovision"/> and in geophysics, including work on seismicity statistics<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Makropoulos|first1=C.|last2=Diagourtas|first2=D.|last3=Liritzis|first3=I.|s2cid=122264625|title=A statistical reappraisal in the relationship between global and Greek seismic activity|journal=Earth, Moon, and Planets|volume=69|issue=1|pages=69–86|issn=0167-9295|doi=10.1007/BF00627771|year=1995|bibcode=1995EM&P...69...69M}}</ref> and archaeomagnetism.

He initiated the Delphi4Delphi International Project.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Liritzis.I.|last2=Pavlidis.G.|last3=Vosynakis.S.|last4=Koutsoudis.A.|last5=Volonakis.P.|last6=Petrochilos.N.|last7=Matthew D. Howland|last8=Brady Liss|last9=Thomas E. Levy|title=DELPHI4DELPHI: first results of the digital archaeology initiative for ancient Delphi, Greece|journal= Antiquity|date=2016|volume=90|issue=354|page=1|article-number=e4 |doi=10.15184/aqy.2016.187|s2cid=164471901|url=https://escholarship.org/content/qt4wq2195j/qt4wq2195j.pdf?t=pqrsbg}}</ref>

Liritzis was elected as a membre correspondent de l'[[Académie des Sciences, Arts et Belles-Lettres de Dijon]]<ref name="ac1"/> and a member of the [[European Academy of Sciences and Arts]].<ref name="ac2"/> He was awarded the Prize of the [[Academy of Athens (modern)|Academy of Athens]] for his book ''Archaeometry: Dating Methods in Archaeology'' (1986) and the [[Costa Navarino]] International Archeometry Award (2010)<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://kalamata.uop.gr/~Archaeolab/AWARD_en.pdf |title=Archived copy |access-date=2011-06-30 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120323234722/http://kalamata.uop.gr/~Archaeolab/AWARD_en.pdf |archive-date=2012-03-23 }}</ref> issued by the University of the Peloponesse.<ref name="kalamata.uop.gr"/> He held visiting positions at Henan University (China),<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hhwm.org/news/list/21 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141108155933/http://hhwm.org/news/list/21 |url-status=dead |archive-date=November 8, 2014 |title=黄河文明中心 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hhwm.org/|title=Examples}}</ref> University of California San Diego,<ref>{{cite web |title=Who we are |website=Center for Cyber-Archaeology & Sustainability at UC San Diego |url=http://ccas.ucsd.edu/who-we-are.php}}</ref> and Edinburgh University.

He is the [[principal investigator]] who initiated and coordinates the Aegean University archaeological excavation project at Delphi<ref>{{cite web|url=https://summer-schools.aegean.gr/KASTROULI2017|title=Home &#124; Summer Schools - University of the Aegean}}</ref> and Kastrouli, a Late Mycenaean site near Delphi, Greece.

The archaeology and history of Egypt was introduced into Greek university curricula in the Department of Mediterranean Studies of the University of the Aegean in 1999. Liritzis established the chair and facilitated the appointment of the first lecturer in Egyptology in 2003. Protocols of collaboration were established between Egyptian universities and the University of the Aegean.<ref>{{cite web |title=Protocol of Collaboration between the University of the Aegean and Helwan University, Egypt |url=http://www1.aegean.gr/international/pdf/MoC_Helwan.pdf}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Protocol of Collaboration between University of the Aegean and Sohag University, Egypt. |url=http://www1.aegean.gr/international/institutional.html}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Protocol of Collaboration between University of the Aegean and Beni Suef University, Egypt |url=https://www1.aegean.gr/international/pdf/MoC_Beni_Suef.pdf}}</ref> The ''[[Heritage (journal)|Heritage]]'' journal published an honorary volume upon his retirement, focusing on his contributions and collaboration with Egyptian researchers on the study of cultural heritage in Egypt.<ref>{{cite journal |title=Essays in Archaeology and Archaeometry and the Hellenic Contribution to Egyptology |journal=Heritage |issue=Special Issue |url=https://www.mdpi.com/journal/heritage/special_issues/egyptology#info |publisher=MDPI}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |author1=University Of The Aegean |year=2001 |title=Gaia Hellenic -Egypt Project |url=https://zenodo.org/records/5998553 |journal=Gaia Hellenic -Egypt Project |language=el, en |doi=10.5281/zenodo.5998553}}</ref>
